sections.title: Habit and leaves
sections.text: Common soapwort is a rhizomatous perennial, usually about 30–90 cm tall, that can form colonies. Its opposite, lance-shaped leaves are about 5–10 cm long; the plate shows the erect stems and pale pink, five-petalled flowers.

sections.title: Flowers and roots
sections.text: Flowers are borne in clusters above the foliage. Creeping underground rhizomes and fleshy roots help the plant spread.

sections.title: Saponins and caution
sections.text: The roots and other tissues contain saponins that foam in water and have been used as a washing agent. Ingestion can be harmful; veterinary toxicology sources report gastrointestinal effects, so soapwort is not a food plant.
